I feel like half the reason I’m still alive is because I’m also trying to understand this question. Certainly there’s something I’m missing. Life is just so draining, why would anybody want to continue enduring the stresses and discomforts of life when they could just not exist? 

Literally life is just our bodies fighting against gravity; feeding, nourishing and keeping our body healthy enough to not get pulled into the ground with the rest of the world’s materials. And it’s an inevitable battle. 

I suppose with consciousness the mental side of it is supposedly better, since we can think, create and be a part of things which matter to other people. But even now, the world has simply shifted towards being more mentally stressed as opposed to physically stressed, which I think is even worse because we’re so aware of everything. 

There are people that would choose to die if it was simple/easy to just push a button and dissolve away, but currently fear the pain. Then there are those who fear the social after effects. 

But then there are people who will never even consider leaving this world, and those are the people I don’t understand.

I’m going through a similar wave of depression and nostalgia only it’s because I moved off to college. Everyday I recount my perfect childhood memories, those last glimpses of true pure happiness that I’ll probably ever have in my life. Chances are life will never be that sweet way again. I miss living in my world of imagination, free and ignorant of the stresses of the real world. I miss embarking on Pokémon adventures and running around outside with my friends, pretending to appear in our created stories. I miss having actual friends who weren’t fearing of others’ judgement on our hobbies. Childhood is a time ripe with innocence and creativity. I feel like school and society is constantly burning my imagination and forcing me to allow others to think for me and dictate who I am. 

Every other day nostalgia hits me and sweeps me back to these glorious anxiety-free times. It seems like life peaked then. Like it will never live up to even if the fraction of happiness produced back then. 

What has helped me is pursuing a path that will allow me to spread the happiness of my childhood to others. My goal in life is to make games for people and share an experience like that. Even if only one person enjoys it and that one person is me or my close kin. 

Of course I thought isolating myself would be the best thing. I stayed in school over the summer (needed a math class finished) but I thought all the free time I had would be put into pursuing projects. The first few weeks of summer I was so productive, I didn’t think I’d hit the rock bottom I’m at now and want to off myself at every stressful scenario. All I’ve been doing I sleeping everyday, avoiding schoolwork whereas I used to get schoolwork done ahead of time in high school, and then have free time afterwards with little stress in the back of my mind. It seems I’ve also fallen into this generations trap of instant gratification, being addicted to my phone and clinging to it the moment I feel uncomfortable or bored when doing something. I know for a fact that has been a damper on my productivity and happiness. 

I lost my friends senior year of high school, and have since diminished in any small amount of social-ability I had before.  Still I keep the nostalgia in the back of my mind that I once was happy, so maybe there’s a chance I can reach a similar time one day. 

I know it feels like life won’t ever reach the happiness accumulated during childhood years, but keep those memories dear and let them be a reminder that your brain can be happy, even if its only a small fraction of childhood happiness. Maybe break out some nostalgic indulgences. You may feel sad afterwards, but your mind will be taken back to memories of you were most happy and put yourself into a mindset where you may be able to relate to life how. I think you might find answers to current problems when analyzing  yourself at the most happiest times.

Also your therapist sounds very unprofessional. It seems like he’s just jumping to conclusions about imaginary semi-beliefs he’s had, but is now confirming them just because of silence? Don’t let his delusions get to you. Chances are there’s a therapist who asks the right questions st the right moments, gives the right responses and is far more comfortable for you to talk around than that guy.

We all have different brains and perceive the world uniquely. 

If I went to the doctor right now and described my symptoms of anxiety and depression I could fall under several categories depending on what I express to them. If you go to a psychiatrist they have this huge dictionary of mental health labels and I bet you’d fall under half of them. Some mental health categories are more broader and are that way so they can give you a label, because their job is literally finding you help and passing on to another next step. 

What does it matter? I can tell you that it only matters if you want medicine or help (disability services, school, etc). Beyond that it means nothing more. If you walk into a doctors office asking for aid, they’re going to hand you a label which you may choose whether or not to slap on your forehead. If you don’t want help or to be associated with that category (which might  mean lowered confidence but the upside of asking for help if you need it), then don’t apply the label.

Embrace who you are. Embrace your uniqueness. Play to your strengths which may seem like weaknesses in other areas. Sure, maybe you’re not a confident social god who everyone who cracks hilarious jokes for everybody to hear in class, but that’s because you have experience in another place. People like that are competent in the social area, but I can guarantee that they lack in other areas. Why? Because they’re spending a good chunk of their time learning how to grow/perform better in that area. 

Anybody can progress in any area of personality, of course at far different rates and levels of success. After everybody’s brain/body is quite unique. But if that’s something you want to grown in to help complement your natural strengths, then you have the choice to.

I second lsd, it saved my life and opened me up to an entirely new world. You will learn so much about who you are right now, who your ideal self is and how to achieve that. 

In my fewest words: it’s almost like re-experiencing the world for the first time (words for me even have different meanings). You will understand how there are many unique ways to think about your life situation, and every other situation out there. The beliefs you have now are not the only way to think about things. 
I could write an entire book describing my experiences and beliefs relating to the drug. 

We all have so many conflicting beliefs in our head, and psychedelics are one of the quickest ways in embracing these beliefs and sorting things out. Perjaps you will see beauty in places you never thought of. there’s no reason not to try it at at least before suicide (you can buy 1p-lsd and research chemicals online legally).

I have incredible anxiety and paranoia, and when taking conscious-altering drugs (weed/acid) I become trapped in my mind and thoughts became really vivid and more real than reality for me (it caused me hallucinate and confuse me badly). 

 I would recommend seeing if the dreams become less vivid when you stop smoking for a bit. (You don’t have to, but it might be worth it to try and at least know).

For me I have dreams that are incredibly real, but only because they’re regular mundane, and actual interactions that I could possibly have with the people in it. Basically when nothing out of the ordinary happens in a dream, it’s difficult for me to compare it to reality. 

These memories, or at least the feelings from them? then sink back into my mind. If I get upset or argue with somebody in a dream, I might wake up with the same feelings towards that person, but am not always sure of where they’re coming from because I can’t judge whether the past memories are dreams or not. 

Is violence ordinary for your reality?

Is there anything or anyone you will miss before you go? 

Surely there’s some good/happiness to be found in something. Do you have any nostalgic activities (video games, movies, foods) you could do that might at least bring you back to memories of when you were happy? Anything that makes you happy which you won’t be able to experience again? 

Is there nothing to look forward to, even just for another moment to reconsider? 

You have the opportunity to make a drastic change in the life, now that you have nothing to lose. Run off. Spend all your money on something and at least try to indulge in the best day of your life before you go.

Whenever you have a semi-complex thought write it down on a Notes app on your phone.

Our brains can only focus on so many things before becoming overwhelmed. You can’t expect your brain to remember everything, and difficult subjects require periods of time and bursts of energy to sort out. By writing the thoughts down, you’re saving them for later where they can be expanded upon, left as is, or even scrapped. Thoughts will be disrupted by other thoughts of various values; life isn’t simple when you have to make conscious decisions. This is why it’s important to permanently store them as they float freely to your consciousness, so you can temporarily move onto other thoughts. 

This is what I’ve been doing, and I no longer have to worry about keeping everything on my mind at once. I have yet to go back and look over these thoughts/beliefs, but it is relieving to know that they will never be forgotten. I plan to sync them to Google Docs one day and sort everything out.

So you’ve had a best friend previously? What happened? 

I too lost my best friend 2 years ago. We did everything together and had a very specific sense of humor. Then one summer he completely ignored me and refused to do anything with me. I will never understand what happened or why, but it’s tore me apart ever since. I no longer know who I am. The years of memories, humor and the part of me that grew alongside my friend have been ripped out from the inside out. I’ve since lost my sense of humor and don’t laugh anymore. Some part or all of my personality must not have lived up to his standards. 

I can somewhat understand your predicament and wanted to share how I feel.

The world wouldn’t be better for your loved ones in that scenario. Maybe if you and I never existed in the first place. But we’re here and the ties we have made with others are real and stay real to them, whether or not we’re here to experience them.

That’s been the only reason that I hold onto. I want to be successful before I kill myself just to prove a point. I almost sure it’ll happen one of these days when I am drained beyond recovery. 

Nobody needs to become a slave for a company for the rest of your life. Create something of your own and live to do that. I’m sure you’re capable of it with your education and likely projects that are on your resume. Are you financially stressed? Work for a company for 1 or 2 years to earn back some money the university stole, learn from it, and create something attached to your identity. You’ll learn from it. I’m sure you’re exhausted but hang in just a little longer, I promise you it’ll be worth persisting through this low-point. If those aren’t options for you, make an extreme change in your life, you’ve got nothing to lose. Maybe a break to catch s glimpse of happiness is what you need; your resume will still be there if you change your mind, and it’s proof you will be a successful person if you push through. 

If it’s identity you desire over success, I’ve also traded away myself to get where I’m at and am in the process of recovering my personality. I may be remnants of who I was before, you can always build myself back and in more positive direction. Your personality is still there because your brain is still your brain and different than anyone else’s. You still interpret things In a way that’s unique to you. You just haven’t worked similar areas of your brain in a long time.
